@aio:claude-modules: ## RBAC
`User → UserRole → Role → RolePermission → Permission → (Resource × Operation)` — a
user holds zero or more roles, each role grants zero or more `(resource, operation)` pairs.
Seeded resources/operations/roles live in `src/seeds/rolesAndPermissions/`: `RESOURCES`
(`src/seeds/rolesAndPermissions/resources.ts`) starts with just `"users"` — add your app's
real nouns there. `OPERATIONS` is the fixed CRUD set (`create`/`read`/`readAll`/`update`/`delete`).
Seeding builds the full resource×operation permission matrix, then grants Admin all of it
and Member read-only — starting points, not a prescription; adjust `roles.ts` for your
actual roles.
**Enforcing it:** `getDomainPermissions(resource)(action)` (`src/middlewares/roleValidator.ts`)
is a curried middleware factory, meant to be partially applied once per route file:
```ts
const hasPermission = getDomainPermissions("widgets");
router.get("/", hasPermission("readAll"), listWidgets);
router.post("/", hasPermission("create"), createWidget);
It runs after `jwtAuth` (needs `res.locals.user`) and throws `ErrorCode.FORBIDDEN` (403) if
the user holds no role granting that `(resource, action)` pair.
**Assigning roles is your call, on purpose:** this module seeds the RBAC tables but never
assigns a role to a newly-registered user — whether every signup gets `Member`, whether
roles are invite-only, whether `Admin` is ever self-service, is a product decision. Wire
`prisma.userRole.create(...)` into `register` (`src/controllers/auth.controller.ts`) once
you've decided.
